assessment: Seelbinder et al. describe a valuable new method for perturbing chromatin in living cells by strongly localized temperature gradients. Solid analysis reveals that chromatin shows both elastic and viscous properties at the timescales of seconds, with heterochromatin showing solid-like properties. While some details of the nuclear response to local heating remain to be elucidated, the ability of the method to reveal local mechanics in vivo makes the approach likely to be of broad interest to both the cell biophysics and cell biology communities.
